hook.text: 23 million Americans live in food deserts—areas where the nearest grocery store is more than a mile away.

buildup.text: In food deserts, the only options are convenience stores and fast food—high in calories, low in nutrition.

discovery.text: Food deserts overlap with poverty and racial segregation. Black and Latino neighborhoods are disproportionately affected.

twist.text: Adding a supermarket doesn't always fix diets. Affordability and food education matter as much as access.

climax.text: Some cities are trying mobile markets, urban farms, and food prescriptions to address gaps.

punchline.text: In the richest country on Earth, millions can't reach a vegetable.

quiz.question: How many Americans live in food deserts?

details.summary: Food deserts are areas where residents have limited access to affordable, nutritious food within a reasonable distance. This topic covers the causes of food deserts, their health consequences, and interventions that bring healthy food to underserved communities.
details.whyItMatters: Millions of people live in areas where the nearest fresh produce is miles away but fast food is on every corner. This inequality drives diet-related diseases in low-income communities.
takeaways: Over 23 million Americans live more than a mile from a supermarket in urban areas
Food deserts correlate strongly with higher rates of obesity and diabetes
Mobile markets, community gardens, and incentive programs are closing access gaps

faq.question: What defines a food desert?
faq.answer: A food desert is typically defined as an area where a significant share of residents live far from a supermarket or grocery store—usually more than one mile in urban areas or ten miles in rural areas—limiting access to fresh, affordable food.

faq.question: What solutions help address food deserts?
faq.answer: Effective interventions include mobile farmers' markets, healthy corner store initiatives, SNAP incentive programs that double purchasing power for produce, community gardens, and zoning policies that encourage grocery store development in underserved areas.
